sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: V5 ICC: surface/membrane localisation of WT-V5 and H991A-V5 are similar (L2). Separately, FLAG-tagged mouse GPR116 (L1) supports Gq/11-coupled IP responses indistinguishable from untagged controls, indicating the N-terminal tag does not disrupt receptor function.
sites.rationale: ADGRF5 has a large N-terminal ectodomain (residues 22–1013) and an intracellular C-terminus; the mature N-terminus after SP cleavage at residue 21 is the only extracellular terminus available for a surface tag. Python confirmed residue 21 = A and residue 22 = A, placing the junction at insert_after_residue = 21. L2 directly confirms extracellular V5 display by ICC on the full-length human receptor; L1 (mouse ortholog, indirect) confirms the N-terminally FLAG-tagged full-length receptor is functionally competent for Gq/11 signalling, together supporting surface_and_function. Full-length human GPR116 (ADGRF5) bearing a V5 tag was transiently expressed in HEK293 cells; V5 immunocytochemistry confirmed membrane/surface localisation of the tagged wild-type receptor. No residue is named in the clip; the C-terminus (residues 1270–1346) is intracellular per topology, leaving the mature N-terminus (after SP cleavage at residue 21) as the sole extracellular terminus. L1 (FLAG-tagged mouse GPR116 ortholog, full-length) independently shows the tagged receptor supports Gq/11-dependent IP signalling, providing corroborating functional evidence for the same junction.

sources.claim: ( B ) Transient expression of V5-tagged H991A in HEK293 cells shows no cleavage at the GPS site by Western blot compared to the wild-type receptor; membrane localization by V5 immunocytochemistry shows similar localization of WT-V5 and H991A-V5.

literature_notes: Only two ledger lines are available (L1, L2). Neither names an explicit residue for the tag insertion; both describe full-length GPR116 constructs whose only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus (after SP cleavage at residue 21), making topology_derived the correct position_evidence. L1 uses mouse GPR116 (indirect ortholog evidence) and demonstrates functional Gq/11 signalling of the FLAG-tagged receptor. L2 uses human GPR116 and confirms surface display by V5 ICC. Because both clips converge on the same unique extracellular terminus, they support a single site rather than two. No internal loop insertions, intracellular tags, or function-abrogating insertions are reported in the ledger; other_positions is therefore empty. H991 mentioned in L2 is the GPS autoproteolysis site studied as a point mutation, not a tag-insertion site, and is not promoted into sites.
